title: Trusted application origins rejected by login preflight
steps: Open customer app; Skip onboarding; enter QA email and password; click Login. Independently OPTIONS /api/v1/auth/login with each verified app Origin, Access-Control-Request-Method: POST, and Access-Control-Request-Headers: content-type.
expected: Explicitly trusted deployed origins receive a valid CORS preflight; browser can submit authentication.
actual: All four current intended app origins return 403 Invalid CORS request with no Access-Control-Allow-Origin. Customer browser reports CORS failure and Network Error.
fix: Correct the exact trusted-origin configuration for staging and its deployed clients. Preserve rejection of untrusted origins.
impact: Customer login and all intended web-to-backend workflows cannot be certified.
frequency: 4/4 intended-origin preflights rejected; customer browser reproduction

title: Deployed client sends authentication to retired backend
steps: Open the specified app; select Email if Plumber; fill the QA login form; submit; inspect the network target.
expected: Authentication targets https://plumbing-qcommerce.onrender.com/api/v1/auth/login.
actual: The app attempts https://fixkart-dev2-backend.onrender.com/api/v1/auth/login. Browser reports CORS/network failure. Admin displays Failed to fetch.
fix: Build and deploy the approved client revision with the intended API base URL; verify actual browser traffic and invalidate stale deployment aliases.
impact: Role cannot log in through its deployed app; cross-app workflow blocked.

title: Enabled Google button exposes missing-config instructions
steps: Skip onboarding; click Continue with Google.
expected: Configured sign-in starts, or an unavailable feature is clearly disabled/explained in user language.
actual: Dialog says Google Client ID missing and instructs user to configure EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID in customer-app/.env.
fix: Configure Google sign-in if in scope; otherwise disable or remove the enabled action and use user-facing copy.
impact: Confusing public auth action; exposes an implementation path, not a secret.

title: Login back arrow has no observable destination
steps: Skip onboarding; click the left arrow on the login screen.
expected: A displayed back action navigates to an available previous screen, or is omitted at the root.
actual: Same login content and URL remain; no dialog or network action.
fix: Remove the root back affordance or connect it to the intended prior screen.
impact: Minor navigation confusion.

title: Invalid and empty authentication forms provide no feedback
steps: Clear mobile field; Continue. Repeat with 123. Switch Email; clear both fields; Continue. Open Sign up; submit empty registration.
expected: Rejected input produces visible, accessible field errors.
actual: No visible message, native dialog, or validating API response; form stays unchanged. Empty registration behaves the same.
fix: Render inline accessible errors in the web build; ensure React Native alerts have a functional web path.
impact: User cannot tell why login/registration does not proceed.
frequency: Repeated blank/short mobile and email/registration checks

title: Empty and partial login/registration forms fail silently
steps: Clear login fields and submit. Open Register Store; submit blank form; enter only manager name and malformed email and resubmit.
expected: Visible, accessible errors identify required/invalid fields.
actual: No visible message or dialog. No registration request is emitted. Adding invalid coordinates to the still-incomplete form also leaves it unchanged; independent coordinate validation remains unverified.
fix: Show field-specific web validation errors and focus the first invalid field.
impact: Store onboarding stalls without explanation.
frequency: Blank registration repeated in two runs

title: OTP screen claims a code was sent without an initial send request
steps: Enter the configured QA plumber mobile number; Continue; inspect the text and network events before verification/resend.
expected: A successful OTP-dispatch response precedes a code-sent message, or the app reports dispatch unavailable.
actual: UI says Enter the 6-digit code sent to the QA number, but initial Continue emits no API request. Verification/resend later target the retired backend and fail.
fix: Connect Continue to the supported OTP-send contract and gate the sent message on success; otherwise disclose deferred OTP support.
impact: Misleading authentication state; user waits for a code whose dispatch was not attempted.

title: Forgot-password and social controls give no feedback
steps: On a fresh login page, click Forgot Password?, Google, and Facebook individually.
expected: An implemented action starts, or deferred support is explained.
actual: Each click leaves text and route unchanged; no dialog or network action is observed.
fix: Wire the actions or expose their unavailable state clearly.
impact: Dead public controls undermine auth usability.

title: Forgot Password control gives no feedback
steps: On store login click Forgot Password?.
expected: Recovery opens, or unavailability/support options are explained.
actual: No route change, dialog, or network action.
fix: Implement the action or provide truthful unavailable/support messaging.
impact: User has no usable recovery guidance.

title: Nine registration inputs have no accessible names
steps: Open Register Store; inspect accessibility tree and run axe WCAG A/AA.
expected: Each input has a programmatically associated name.
actual: Axe label rule flags 9 inputs (critical impact); no label, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, or placeholder provides their names.
fix: Associate each visible label with its input and verify the computed accessible name.
impact: Screen-reader users cannot reliably identify registration fields.

title: Five registration inputs have no accessible names
steps: Click the exact Sign up link; inspect the form with axe/accessibility tree.
expected: Every input has a meaningful accessible name.
actual: Axe label rule flags all 5 registration inputs (critical impact).
fix: Associate labels and provide correct text/telephone/password input semantics.
impact: Plumber registration is inaccessible to users relying on accessible field names.

title: Six OTP inputs have no accessible names
steps: Enter QA mobile; Continue; inspect each OTP textbox using axe/accessibility tree.
expected: OTP digits have distinct names or a single clearly labeled code input.
actual: All 6 OTP inputs fail the label rule (critical impact).
fix: Use a labeled single code input or uniquely label each digit and preserve focus behavior.
impact: OTP entry cannot be reliably interpreted by a screen reader.

title: Small supporting text falls below 4.5:1 contrast
steps: Open email login and OTP screens; run axe color-contrast rule.
expected: Normal small text reaches at least 4.5:1.
actual: or continue with and Your data is safe with us are reported at 4.26:1 (#727785 on #faf9fd), 12px.
fix: Darken the supporting text color and retest all affected backgrounds.
impact: Reduced readability for low-vision users.

title: Tabs and remember control lack roles/state; Sign up is absent from tab loop
steps: Inspect the login accessibility tree; Tab and Shift+Tab through the controls; toggle Remember me.
expected: Tabs expose selected state, checkbox exposes checked state, and Sign up is keyboard reachable.
actual: Tabs/remember are focusable divs without roles or selected/checked semantics. The captured tab cycle omits the inline Sign up link, although exact pointer click opens registration.
fix: Use appropriate interactive roles, states, and keyboard activation; make Sign up a link/button.
impact: Keyboard and assistive-technology users receive incomplete control information.

title: Public mobile-web aliases are behind backend and repository HEAD
steps: Compare Vercel production alias metadata for customer/plumber/store with backend /version and local Development-2 HEAD.
expected: Certification targets identify the same approved release, or an explicitly approved compatibility set.
actual: All three mobile-web production aliases point to cf3fab03; backend/local HEAD is 618a8181. Ready previews at HEAD do not prove production aliases were updated.
fix: Align and approve the deployment set, then repeat the entire browser suite against the actual release aliases.
impact: Current audit cannot certify Development-2 HEAD as the deployed ecosystem.

title: Development-2 admin build failed; old branch remains live
steps: Inspect Vercel admin latest deployment and production alias metadata.
expected: Approved Development-2 admin build is healthy and deployed.
actual: Latest HEAD build is ERROR with missing_pages_app / npm run vercel-build exited 1. Production remains 99a19057 from phase13a-local-staging-sms, with gitDirty=1 in metadata.
fix: Correct build root/framework commands, produce a reproducible clean build, and deploy the approved revision.
impact: Current role administration and least-privilege implementation cannot be certified.

title: Runbook admin URL points to a different authentication surface
steps: Open runbook URL https://fixkart-admin.vercel.app and compare with Vercel project domains.
expected: Runbook identifies the repository-owned deployed admin portal.
actual: Runbook URL redirects to Clerk development sign-in; actual repository project alias is admin-portal-ten-weld.vercel.app.
fix: Update canonical environment documentation after confirming the intended admin release URL.
impact: QA/operators may inspect the wrong admin environment.

title: Repository QA fallback does not authenticate live seeded accounts
steps: Securely resolve the existing QA credential configuration; attempt one direct login for customer.qa, plumber.qa, store.qa, and admin.qa on the intended backend.
expected: Approved staging QA credentials establish the expected identities.
actual: All four return 401 Invalid credentials. APP_SEED_DEMO_PASSWORD is absent in the process environment; the one existing historical-script value tried is stale/unusable. Startup logs confirm staging seeders ran. No further password guesses were attempted.
fix: Provide the current approved QA secret through a secure local/environment source; do not re-enable an old public default or alter account roles to make tests pass.
impact: Authenticated APIs, IDOR, session lifecycle, business workflows and persistence remain blocked.
frequency: 1 direct attempt per configured QA account; 4/4 rejected
